name: Key Summit Track
why: An hour up the Routeburn Track from the Milford Road and a short climb to alpine tarns and bogs, with views over the Hollyford Valley to the Humboldt and Darran Mountains.
book: Free, no booking for a day walk. The Divide car park is about 85 km from Te Anau on the Milford Road (SH94).
dangers: Fiordland weather: heavy rain, wind and cold arrive fast; in cloud there is no view from the top.
Boardwalks and rock can be slippery when wet.
turnaround: If Key Summit is in cloud at the turn-off, skip the last 20 minutes: there will be nothing to see.

points.name: The Divide
points.note: Shelter and car park on the Milford Road at 531 m. The first hour follows the Routeburn Track through silver beech.

points.name: Key Summit tarns
points.note: 918 m. Tarns and bog on an ice-scoured knob; a glacier once overtopped it by 500 m. Return the same way.
